rule.name: Database queries should not be vulnerable to injection attacks
rule.riskDescription: SQL injection occurs when untrusted data is concatenated into a SQL query without proper escaping. An attacker can manipulate the query to gain unauthorized access or destroy data.
rule.vulnerabilityDescription:
Building queries via string concatenation makes it possible to inject malicious SQL. The application must validate and sanitize untrusted inputs before using them in SQL queries.

Affected queries should be reviewed and rewritten as parameterized statements.
rule.fixRecommendations:
Use parameterized queries (PreparedStatement in Java) to keep data and code separate.

PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
stmt.setInt(1, userId);

If parameterization is impossible, validate the input against a strict allowlist.
